need to install next, apt install -y build-essential linux-headers=$(uname -r) vlan libaiol . then install host modules from /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware/vmware-host-modules using make , make install . vmware bundle file is in /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware/*.bundle . remember, we need same method as the apt install again Weighing header paths and safer module install options. Same method — download-only, extract, no writes to the broken /usr/lib. One correction on package naming first: it's linux-headers-$(uname -r) (hyphen, not =) — the = syntax would try to pin the generic linux-headers package to a version string that doesn't exist. 1 — Download everything (including all dependencies) without installing: bash

text
apt install --download-only -y build-essential linux-headers-$(uname -r) vlan libaio1

2 — Extract every downloaded .deb into the same persistent lib-ext tree: bash

text
for pkg in /var/cache/apt/archives/*.deb; do
    dpkg-deb -x "$pkg" /data/lib-ext
done

3 — Broaden the linker path (build-essential's libs land in more places than lvm2's did): bash

text
cat > /etc/ld.so.conf.d/dsl-persist.conf << 'EOF'
/data/lib-ext/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu
/data/lib-ext/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu
/data/lib-ext/usr/lib
/data/lib-ext/lib
EOF
ldconfig

4 — Symlink binaries into the working /usr/sbin overlay (same clean, sda2-backed mount we already have — don't use /usr/bin, it's never been overlaid and is still the read-only base): bash

text
for f in /data/lib-ext/usr/bin/* /data/lib-ext/bin/*; do
    ln -sf "$f" "/usr/sbin/$(basename "$f")" 2>/dev/null
done
gcc --version
make --version

One real snag to expect: gcc may run but fail to find its internal helper (cc1) when actually compiling, since that lives in a versioned subdirectory (/data/lib-ext/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/12/) that a bare symlink doesn't expose correctly. Test before moving to the kernel build: bash

text
echo 'int main(){return 0;}' > /tmp/test.c
gcc /tmp/test.c -o /tmp/test

If that errors with cc1: not found, tell me and I'll give you the -B flag / wrapper-script fix — don't want to hand you a broken toolchain right before a kernel module build. 5 — VMware host modules build. This is where it gets genuinely tricky: the module Makefile normally finds kernel headers via /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build, but that symlink lives under /usr/lib — the same directory whose overlay is still broken from earlier tonight. Bypass it by pointing directly at the extracted headers instead: bash

text
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware/vmware-host-modules
make VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) KERNEL_DIR=/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-$(uname                   Linux flex 6.1.0-50-amd64 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Debian 6.1.176-1 (2026-07-02) x86_64

The make failed because the expected source layout is missing.
A proper vmware-host-modules tree (from mkubecek or the version-matched tarball) must contain the sub-directories vmmon-only and vmnet-only. Your current directory does not.

1. Inspect what you actually have

Run these and paste the output:

Bash

ls -la /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware/vmware-host-modules/ 2>/dev/null || echo "directory missing or empty"
find /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware -maxdepth 3 -type d | head -40
ls /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware/*.bundle 2>/dev/null

2. Most likely fix – get a correct source tree

The cleanest “same method” way (no writes into the broken /usr tree) is to pull the matching branch from mkubecek and keep everything under /data:

Bash
# pick the branch that matches your VMware version
# (check with strings on the .bundle or look inside /etc/vmware/config if it exists)
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware
git clone --depth 1 -b workstation-17.6.0 https://github.com/mkubecek/vmware-host-modules.git vmware-host-modules-clean
# ← change the branch name to the exact version you have (17.5.2, 17.6.1, etc.)

cd vmware-host-modules-clean
ls -d vmmon-only vmnet-only   # both must appear

If you already have a version-matched tarball or zip, just unpack it under /data the same way.

3. Build with the extracted headers (no broken /lib/modules symlink)

Bash
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware/vmware-host-modules-clean   # or whatever the good tree is

make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR=/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-$(uname -r)

If the headers path is slightly different (common with the extracted debs), locate it first:

Bash
find /data/lib-ext -type d -name 'linux-headers-*' | head

and adjust KERNEL_DIR= accordingly.

4. Install the modules into a safe location

Because /lib/modules and /usr/lib are still broken, install into a temporary tree and then load manually:

Bash
make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR=/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-$(uname -r) \
  DESTDIR=/data/vmware-modules \
  install

Then:

Bash
# copy the .ko files to a place depmod / modprobe can see them
mkdir -p /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/misc
cp -v /data/vmware-modules/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/misc/*.ko /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/misc/
depmod -a $(uname -r)

# load them
modprobe vmmon
modprobe vmnet
lsmod | grep -E 'vmmon|vmnet'

2. Extract the .bundle without letting it install system-wide

The .bundle is a self-extracting script. We force it to dump its payload into our tree:

Bash
BUNDLE=$(ls /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware/*.bundle | head -1)
echo "Using: $BUNDLE"

# Make it executable
chmod +x "$BUNDLE"

# Extract only (no install). The --extract flag dumps the payload.
# Destination must be absolute and under /data
"$BUNDLE" --extract /data/vmware-root/extract

If --extract is not accepted by your particular bundle version, use the older method:

Bash
# Alternative extraction (works on almost every VMware .bundle)
mkdir -p /data/vmware-root/extract
cd /data/vmware-root/extract
"$BUNDLE" --console --required --eulas-agreed --ignore-errors \
  --set-setting=vmware-installer installComponents false 2>/dev/null || true
# If it still tries to install, kill it and we’ll do a pure tar-style extract next

After extraction you should see something like:

text
/data/vmware-root/extract/vmware-installer
/data/vmware-root/extract/vmware-vix
/data/vmware-root/extract/vmware-player   (or workstation)
...

3. Relocate the extracted tree into a permanent prefix

Bash
# Move the real product files into a clean prefix
mv /data/vmware-root/extract/* /data/vmware-root/ 2>/dev/null || true
# or, if the layout is nested:
# find /data/vmware-root/extract -maxdepth 2 -type d

We will later set VMWARE_PREFIX=/data/vmware-root (or whatever the final layout is) so all binaries, modules, and libraries stay there.

The --extract flag did nothing useful on this 16.2.4 bundle (common with older ones). We’ll force a pure payload dump under /data/vmware-root and keep going with the modules.

1. Extract the bundle the reliable way

Bash
cd /data/vmware-root
BUNDLE=/data/vmware-root/VMware-Workstation-Full-16.2.4-20089737.x86_64.bundle
chmod +x "$BUNDLE"

# Create a clean extract directory
rm -rf extract
mkdir extract
cd extract

# Run the installer in “extract-only” style.
# We deliberately feed it settings that stop it from writing outside /data
"$BUNDLE" --console --eulas-agreed --required \
  --set-setting=vmware-installer installComponents false \
  --set-setting=vmware-installer prefix /data/vmware-root/product \
  2>&1 | tee /tmp/bundle-run.log

If it still tries to install system-wide or hangs, kill it (Ctrl-C) and use the binary-extraction fallback:

Bash
# Fallback – treat the .bundle as a self-extracting archive
cd /data/vmware-root
mkdir -p extract2
# The payload is a compressed archive after the shell script header
# Skip the script part and untar
tail -n +$(grep -a -n '^__ARCHIVE_BELOW__' "$BUNDLE" | cut -d: -f1) "$BUNDLE" | \
  tar -xzf - -C extract2 2>/dev/null || \
  # some bundles use a different marker
  dd if="$BUNDLE" bs=1M skip=1 2>/dev/null | tar -xzf - -C extract2 2>/dev/null

ls extract2 | head
find extract2 -maxdepth 2 -type d | head -15

Two problems:

  1. HEADERS= is empty — the headers directory was never found.
  2. There are already-built .ko files from a completely different kernel (RHEL 5.14), so the install step refuses them.

We fix both.

1. Find the real headers path

Bash

# also check the common extracted locations
ls -d /data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-* 2>/dev/null
ls -d /data/lib-ext/usr/src/* 2>/dev/null
ls -d /data/lib-ext/lib/modules/*/build 2>/dev/null

Paste the output of those four commands.
(While you do that, the rest of the steps below are ready.)

2. Once we have a real HEADERS path

HEADERS=/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64   # ← example, use the real one

echo "Using: $HEADERS"
ls "$HEADERS"/Makefile "$HEADERS"/include  # both must exist

3. Clean + rebuild from scratch (ignore the old .ko files)

Bash
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware-install-files/vmware-host-modules-workstation-16.2.4

# remove the wrong-kernel objects
rm -f vmmon.o vmnet.o
rm -rf vmmon-only/vmmon.ko vmnet-only/vmnet.ko
make clean

# build against the Debian 6.1 headers we extracted
make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR="$HEADERS" \
  DESTDIR=/data/vmware-modules

this is how headers were (or must) be installed 1 — Download everything (including all dependencies) without installing: bash

text
apt install --download-only -y build-essential linux-headers-$(uname -r) vlan libaio1

2 — Extract every downloaded .deb into the same persistent lib-ext tree: bash

text
for pkg in /var/cache/apt/archives/*.deb; do
    dpkg-deb -x "$pkg" /data/lib-ext
done

3 — Broaden the linker path (build-essential's libs land in more places than lvm2's did): bash

text
cat > /etc/ld.so.conf.d/dsl-persist.conf << 'EOF'
/data/lib-ext/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu
/data/lib-ext/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu
/data/lib-ext/usr/lib
/data/lib-ext/lib
EOF
ldconfig

4 — Symlink binaries into the working /usr/sbin overlay (same clean, sda2-backed mount we already have — don't use /usr/bin, it's never been overlaid and is still the read-only base): bash

text
for f in /data/lib-ext/usr/bin/* /data/lib-ext/bin/*; do
    ln -sf "$f" "/usr/sbin/$(basename "$f")" 2>/dev/null
done

The headers for the running kernel (6.1.0-50-amd64) never landed in /data/lib-ext.
What is there is only the RT kernel 6.1.0-53-rt-amd64 (and no build / linux-headers-* tree at all).

We have to re-download + extract the correct packages the same way you did before.

1. Download the exact headers that match the running kernel

Bash
# confirm the running kernel
uname -r
# must print 6.1.0-50-amd64

# download only (no install)
apt install --download-only -y \
  linux-headers-$(uname -r) \
  linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common \
  linux-kbuild-6.1 \
  linux-compiler-gcc-12-x86 \
  build-essential

If apt complains about held packages again, add --allow-change-held-packages.

2. Extract every newly downloaded .deb into the same persistent tree

Bash
# only the packages we just fetched
for pkg in /var/cache/apt/archives/linux-headers-*.deb \
           /var/cache/apt/archives/linux-kbuild-*.deb \
           /var/cache/apt/archives/linux-compiler-*.deb \
           /var/cache/apt/archives/build-essential*.deb \
           /var/cache/apt/archives/g++*.deb \
           /var/cache/apt/archives/gcc*.deb \
           /var/cache/apt/archives/dpkg-dev*.deb \
           /var/cache/apt/archives/libc6-dev*.deb \
           /var/cache/apt/archives/linux-libc-dev*.deb; do
    [ -f "$pkg" ] && dpkg-deb -x "$pkg" /data/lib-ext
done

3. Verify the headers are now present

Bash
find /data/lib-ext -type d -name 'linux-headers-6.1.0-50*' 
ls -d /data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64
ls /data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/Makefile

You must see the directory and a Makefile inside it.

4. Point the module build at the real headers

Bash
HEADERS=/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64
echo "HEADERS=$HEADERS"
ls "$HEADERS"/Makefile "$HEADERS"/include

5. Rebuild the modules cleanly

Bash
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware-install-files/vmware-host-modules-workstation-16.2.4

# wipe any previous wrong-kernel objects
rm -f vmmon.o vmnet.o
rm -rf vmmon-only/*.ko vmnet-only/*.ko
make clean

make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR="$HEADERS" \
  DESTDIR=/data/vmware-modules

make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR="$HEADERS" \
  DESTDIR=/data/vmware-modules \
  install

6. Confirm and load

Bash

modinfo /data/vmware-modules/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/misc/vmmon.ko | grep vermagic
# must say 6.1.0-50-amd64

echo "/data/vmware-modules/lib/modules/$(uname -r)" > /etc/depmod.d/99-vmware-data.conf
depmod -a $(uname -r)

modprobe -S $(uname -r) vmnet
lsmod | grep -E 'vmmon|vmnet'

Diagnose the headers tree

Bash
HEADERS=/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64
echo "=== top level ==="
ls -la "$HEADERS"
echo "=== include ==="
ls -la "$HEADERS/include"
echo "=== generated ==="
ls -la "$HEADERS/include/generated" 2>/dev/null || echo "no generated"
echo "=== looking for autoconf.h ==="
find "$HEADERS" -name 'autoconf.h' 2>/dev/null
echo "=== common headers ==="
ls -d /data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common 2>/dev/null
ls /data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common/include 2>/dev/null | head

Also extract the remaining packages that were downloaded earlier

Bash
# make sure the common + kbuild + compiler packages are fully extracted
for pkg in /var/cache/apt/archives/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common*.deb \
           /var/cache/apt/archives/linux-kbuild-6.1*.deb \
           /var/cache/apt/archives/linux-compiler-gcc-12-x86*.deb \
           /var/cache/apt/archives/linux-libc-dev*.deb; do
    [ -f "$pkg" ] && echo "Extracting $pkg" && dpkg-deb -x "$pkg" /data/lib-ext
done

Re-run the diagnose block above after the extra extracts.

Headers look good now (autoconf.h is present). The VMware Makefile is falling back to its “standalone” build system and not finding the generated headers correctly.

Force it to use the proper kernel build system and give it the full include path.

1. Create the classic modules/build symlink under /data

Bash
mkdir -p /data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)
ln -sfn /data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64 \
        /data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build
ln -sfn /data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common \
        /data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/source

# also fix the relative scripts/tools links if they are broken
ls -l /data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/scripts
ls -l /data/lib-ext/usr/lib/linux-kbuild-6.1/scripts 2>/dev/null || \
  ls -l /data/lib-ext/lib/linux-kbuild-6.1/scripts 2>/dev/null

2. Rebuild with explicit kernel build system

Bash
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware-install-files/vmware-host-modules-workstation-16.2.4

make clean

# force the kernel build system (not standalone)
make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR=/data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build \
  HEADER_DIR=/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64 \
  DESTDIR=/data/vmware-modules \
  -j$(nproc)

If it still complains about generated/autoconf.h, add the include path explicitly:

Bash
make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR=/data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build \
  EXTRA_CFLAGS="-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include -I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include/generated" \
  DESTDIR=/data/vmware-modules

3. If the above still fails, try the classic “make -C” style that VMware expects

Bash
# some older 16.x trees prefer this
make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KDIR=/data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build \
  DESTDIR=/data/vmware-modules

The Makefile is still forcing the standalone build path, which does not receive the correct include directories from KERNEL_DIR. We need to either patch the detection or supply the missing include path directly.

Fix 1 – force the kernel build system by setting the expected variables

Bash
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware-install-files/vmware-host-modules-workstation-16.2.4

# clean again
make clean 2>/dev/null || true
rm -rf vmmon-only/*.o vmnet-only/*.o

# explicit environment that the VMware Makefiles look for
export KERNEL_DIR=/data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build
export KDIR=$KERNEL_DIR
export VM_UNAME=$(uname -r)

# try with the classic make -C style that older 16.x trees understand
make -C vmmon-only \
  KERNEL_DIR=$KERNEL_DIR \
  KDIR=$KERNEL_DIR \
  VM_UNAME=$VM_UNAME \
  HEADER_DIR=/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64

Fix 2 – if it still says “standalone”, inject the include path

Bash
# add the missing include so standalone can find generated/autoconf.h
make -C vmmon-only \
  KERNEL_DIR=$KERNEL_DIR \
  EXTRA_CFLAGS="-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include -I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include/generated -I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common/include" \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r)

Do the same for vmnet-only once vmmon-only succeeds.

Fix 3 – quick patch to the detection logic (most reliable)

The standalone detection is controlled by the presence of certain files. We can temporarily make it think a proper kernel build directory exists:

Bash
# create a minimal marker that some 16.x Makefiles check
touch /data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build/include/linux/version.h 2>/dev/null || \
  ln -s /data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common/include/linux/version.h \
        /data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build/include/linux/version.h 2>/dev/null

# also make sure the relative scripts link resolves from the build dir
ls -l /data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/scripts
# it points to ../../lib/linux-kbuild-6.1/scripts – verify that target exists
ls /data/lib-ext/lib/linux-kbuild-6.1/scripts | head

Then re-run:

Bash
make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR=/data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build \
  DESTDIR=/data/vmware-modules

The autoconf.h problem is fixed.
The new failure is because DESTDIR=/data/vmware-modules is being treated as the build directory by the standalone Makefile (it cds into it and then looks for ../Makefile).

Do not pass DESTDIR on the build step — only on the install step.

Clean + build without DESTDIR

Bash
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware-install-files/vmware-host-modules-workstation-16.2.4

make clean
rm -rf vmmon-only/driver-* vmnet-only/driver-* 2>/dev/null

export KERNEL_DIR=/data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build
export KDIR=$KERNEL_DIR
export VM_UNAME=$(uname -r)

# BUILD only – no DESTDIR
make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR=$KERNEL_DIR \
  EXTRA_CFLAGS="-fno-PIC -fno-PIE"

If that succeeds you should see vmmon-only/vmmon.ko and vmnet-only/vmnet.ko.

Then install into /data only

Bash
make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR=$KERNEL_DIR \
  DESTDIR=/data/vmware-modules \
  install

Verify

Bash
find /data/vmware-modules -name '*.ko' -ls
modinfo vmmon-only/vmmon.ko | grep vermagic

The EXTRA_CFLAGS is not reaching the compiler in the standalone Makefile. Force it harder.

Override the CFLAGS that the standalone system uses

Bash
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware-install-files/vmware-host-modules-workstation-16.2.4

make clean
rm -rf vmmon-only/driver-* vmnet-only/driver-* 2>/dev/null

export KERNEL_DIR=/data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build
export KDIR=$KERNEL_DIR
export VM_UNAME=$(uname -r)

# force the flags that the standalone Makefile actually respects
make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR=$KERNEL_DIR \
  CC="gcc -fno-PIC -fno-PIE" \
  CFLAGS="-fno-PIC -fno-PIE -mcmodel=kernel" \
  EXTRA_CFLAGS="-fno-PIC -fno-PIE -mcmodel=kernel"

If it still complains, edit the Makefile that is generating the bad flags:

Bash
# find where -fPIC or the code-model is being set
grep -n -E 'PIC|PIE|mcmodel|code.model' vmmon-only/Makefile* vmmon-only/Makefile.normal 2>/dev/null | head -20

Locate it

Bash

find . -name 'cpu_types*.h' 2>/dev/null

ls vmmon-only/common/ 2>/dev/null | head

Quick fix once we know where it lives

Most of the time it is under vmmon-only/include/ or an arch subdir. If it exists:

Bash
# example – adjust path from the find above
ls -l vmmon-only/include/cpu_types_arch.h
# if it is missing, it may be generated or in a different tree

If the file is present but the include path is wrong, add it the same way we fixed autoconf.h:

Bash
# show the include line
sed -n '35,45p' vmmon-only/include/cpu_types.h

Then either:

Bash
# absolute include (same style as before)
sed -i 's|#include "cpu_types_arch.h"|#include "/full/path/to/cpu_types_arch.h"|' \
  vmmon-only/include/cpu_types.h

or create a symlink in the place the compiler is looking.

The -I flags are still not reaching the actual compiler invocation. The standalone Makefile ignores CFLAGS/EXTRA_CFLAGS for the final compile step.

Force them by editing the Makefile that drives the compile, or by setting the include path the way the standalone system expects.

Quick permanent fix – patch the Makefile.normal that is used

Bash
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware-install-files/vmware-host-modules-workstation-16.2.4

# see how it builds
grep -n 'CFLAGS\|INCLUDE\| -I' vmmon-only/Makefile.normal | head -20

Stronger approach – set the environment variables the standalone system actually reads

Many of these old VMware standalone Makefiles look for LINUXINCLUDE or put includes in CPPFLAGS:

Bash
export KERNEL_DIR=/data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build
export KDIR=$KERNEL_DIR
export VM_UNAME=$(uname -r)

export CPPFLAGS="-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include \
-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include/generated \
-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common/include \
-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common/include/uapi \
-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/arch/x86/include \
-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/arch/x86/include/generated"

export CFLAGS="-fno-PIC -fno-PIE -mcmodel=kernel $CPPFLAGS"
export EXTRA_CFLAGS="$CFLAGS"
export CC="gcc -fno-PIC -fno-PIE"

make clean
rm -rf vmmon-only/driver-* vmnet-only/driver-* 2>/dev/null

make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR=$KERNEL_DIR \
  CC="$CC" \
  CFLAGS="$CFLAGS" \
  EXTRA_CFLAGS="$EXTRA_CFLAGS" \
  CPPFLAGS="$CPPFLAGS"

If that still fails, we edit Makefile.normal directly to hard-code the -I lines.

Paste the output of the grep on Makefile.normal and the next make attempt.

The Makefile uses its own INCLUDE variable that only looks at HEADER_DIR. We set that and also hard-point the one include that is failing.

1. Set HEADER_DIR and force INCLUDE

Bash
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware-install-files/vmware-host-modules-workstation-16.2.4

export KERNEL_DIR=/data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build
export KDIR=$KERNEL_DIR
export VM_UNAME=$(uname -r)
export HEADER_DIR=/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common

# also make the one failing include absolute (same style as autoconf)
sed -i 's|#include <linux/file.h>|#include "/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common/include/linux/file.h"|' \
  vmmon-only/linux/driver.c

2. Rebuild

Bash
make clean
rm -rf vmmon-only/driver-* vmnet-only/driver-* 2>/dev/null

make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR=$KERNEL_DIR \
  HEADER_DIR=$HEADER_DIR \
  CC="gcc -fno-PIC -fno-PIE" \
  CFLAGS="-fno-PIC -fno-PIE -mcmodel=kernel" \
  EXTRA_CFLAGS="-fno-PIC -fno-PIE -mcmodel=kernel"

The HEADER_DIR is what the Makefile actually appends to INCLUDE. Combined with the absolute path for file.h, this should get past the current error.

Absolute path on one file will keep cascading. Fix the real include path in the Makefile so the whole kernel header tree is visible.

1. Patch Makefile.normal to include the full set of header directories

Bash
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware-install-files/vmware-host-modules-workstation-16.2.4

# backup
cp vmmon-only/Makefile.normal vmmon-only/Makefile.normal.bak

# expand the INCLUDE line
sed -i 's|INCLUDE := -I$(SRCROOT)/include -I$(SRCROOT)/common -I$(SRCROOT)/linux \\|INCLUDE := -I$(SRCROOT)/include -I$(SRCROOT)/common -I$(SRCROOT)/linux \\\n\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common/include \\\n\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common/include/uapi \\\n\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include \\\n\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include/generated \\\n\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/arch/x86/include \\\n\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/arch/x86/include/generated \\|' \
  vmmon-only/Makefile.normal

# also do the same for vmnet if it has the same file
cp vmnet-only/Makefile.normal vmnet-only/Makefile.normal.bak 2>/dev/null || true
sed -i 's|INCLUDE := -I$(SRCROOT)/include -I$(SRCROOT)/common -I$(SRCROOT)/linux \\|INCLUDE := -I$(SRCROOT)/include -I$(SRCROOT)/common -I$(SRCROOT)/linux \\\n\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common/include \\\n\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common/include/uapi \\\n\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include \\\n\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include/generated \\\n\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/arch/x86/include \\\n\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/arch/x86/include/generated \\|' \
  vmnet-only/Makefile.normal 2>/dev/null || true

2. Revert the absolute include we added earlier (so it uses the normal search path)

Bash
sed -i 's|#include "/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common/include/linux/file.h"|#include <linux/file.h>|' \
  vmmon-only/linux/driver.c

3. Rebuild

Bash
make clean
rm -rf vmmon-only/driver-* vmnet-only/driver-* 2>/dev/null

export KERNEL_DIR=/data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build
export HEADER_DIR=/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common

make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR=$KERNEL_DIR \
  HEADER_DIR=$HEADER_DIR \
  CC="gcc -fno-PIC -fno-PIE" \
  CFLAGS="-fno-PIC -fno-PIE -mcmodel=kernel" \
  EXTRA_CFLAGS="-fno-PIC -fno-PIE -mcmodel=kernel"

This puts every needed kernel header directory into INCLUDE once and for all. Paste the next error if any.

These errors mean the standalone build is compiling kernel headers without the proper generated config and architecture defines. That is why IS_ENABLED(), MAX_ORDER, etc. blow up.

We need to force the real kernel build system instead of the broken standalone path.

Force the kernel build system

Bash
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware-install-files/vmware-host-modules-workstation-16.2.4

# restore the original Makefile.normal (we edited it)
cp vmmon-only/Makefile.normal.bak vmmon-only/Makefile.normal 2>/dev/null || true
cp vmnet-only/Makefile.normal.bak vmnet-only/Makefile.normal 2>/dev/null || true

# make sure the build symlink is correct
ls -l /data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build

# the key: use the kernel's own make system
make clean
rm -rf vmmon-only/driver-* vmnet-only/driver-* 2>/dev/null

# this is the classic way that actually works with modern kernels
make \
  -C /data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build \
  M=$(pwd)/vmmon-only \
  modules \
  EXTRA_CFLAGS="-fno-PIC -fno-PIE"

If that still refuses, try the version that many people use for 16.x on newer kernels:

Bash
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware-install-files/vmware-host-modules-workstation-16.2.4

# force the kernel build system by creating the expected marker
touch /data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build/.config

# and run with the variables the top-level Makefile understands
make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR=/data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build \
  HEADER_DIR=/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64 \
  CC="gcc -fno-PIC -fno-PIE" \
  CFLAGS="-fno-PIC -fno-PIE -mcmodel=kernel"

Run the first block (the -C ... M=... modules form) and paste the full output. That is the path that actually feeds the kernel headers the config macros they need.

The kernel headers themselves are broken for out-of-tree use because their internal Makefile points at the real /usr/src/... path that doesn’t exist.

Fix the kernel headers’ internal path

Bash
# the headers Makefile is looking for the common tree in the wrong place
ls -l /data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/Makefile

# show what it is trying to include
head -5 /data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/Makefile

Most Debian header packages have a line like:

make
include /usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common/Makefile

We rewrite it to the real location under /data:

Bash
sed -i 's|/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common|/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common|g' \
  /data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/Makefile

# also fix any other absolute /usr/src references that may exist
grep -r '/usr/src/linux-headers' /data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/ --include='Makefile*' | head

Now force the kernel build system again

Bash
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware-install-files/vmware-host-modules-workstation-16.2.4

make clean
rm -rf vmmon-only/driver-* 2>/dev/null

make \
  -C /data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build \
  M=$(pwd)/vmmon-only \
  modules \
  EXTRA_CFLAGS="-fno-PIC -fno-PIE"

If the sed worked, the “No such file or directory” for the common Makefile should disappear and we will get real kernel-style compilation.

You're right — we were further along with the standalone path. Let's go back to that and fix the include path properly so it doesn't cascade.

Restore and properly patch the standalone Makefile

Bash
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware-install-files/vmware-host-modules-workstation-16.2.4

# restore clean Makefile.normal
cp vmmon-only/Makefile.normal.bak vmmon-only/Makefile.normal 2>/dev/null || true

# show the current INCLUDE lines
sed -n '65,75p' vmmon-only/Makefile.normal

Hard-code the full include path into Makefile.normal

Bash
# replace the INCLUDE definition with a complete one
cat > /tmp/include_fix.txt << 'EOF'
INCLUDE := -I$(SRCROOT)/include -I$(SRCROOT)/common -I$(SRCROOT)/linux \
        -I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common/include \
        -I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common/include/uapi \
        -I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include \
        -I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include/generated \
        -I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/arch/x86/include \
        -I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/arch/x86/include/generated \
        -I$(HEADER_DIR)
EOF

# apply it (this overwrites the old INCLUDE block)
sed -i '/^INCLUDE :=/,+1c\
INCLUDE := -I$(SRCROOT)/include -I$(SRCROOT)/common -I$(SRCROOT)/linux \\\
\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common/include \\\
\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common/include/uapi \\\
\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include \\\
\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include/generated \\\
\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/arch/x86/include \\\
\t-I/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/arch/x86/include/generated \\\
\t-I$(HEADER_DIR)' vmmon-only/Makefile.normal

Also fix the absolute include we may have left in driver.c

Bash
sed -i 's|#include "/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common/include/linux/file.h"|#include <linux/file.h>|' \
  vmmon-only/linux/driver.c 2>/dev/null || true

Rebuild with standalone

Bash
make clean
rm -rf vmmon-only/driver-* 2>/dev/null

export KERNEL_DIR=/data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build
export HEADER_DIR=/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common

make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR=$KERNEL_DIR \
  HEADER_DIR=$HEADER_DIR \
  CC="gcc -fno-PIC -fno-PIE" \
  CFLAGS="-fno-PIC -fno-PIE -mcmodel=kernel" \
  EXTRA_CFLAGS="-fno-PIC -fno-PIE -mcmodel=kernel"

These are preprocessor failures because the kernel headers are being compiled without the config macros that IS_ENABLED() and the size checks need.

The fix is to force the generated config headers in first.

1. Make sure the generated autoconf is visible and force it early

Bash
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware-install-files/vmware-host-modules-workstation-16.2.4

# confirm the file
ls /data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include/generated/autoconf.h

# force the standalone system to pull in the config before anything else
# by prepending it to the INCLUDE list we already patched

2. Add the critical defines that stop the cascade

The IS_ENABLED errors and the MAX_ORDER / SECTION_SIZE errors happen when CONFIG_* macros are missing. We can feed them via EXTRA_CFLAGS / CFLAGS the same way the kernel does:

Bash
export KERNEL_DIR=/data/lib-ext/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build
export HEADER_DIR=/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common

# these two defines are what the kernel build system injects
# and what the standalone path is missing
EXTRA_DEFINES="-include /data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include/generated/autoconf.h \
-D__KERNEL__ \
-DKBUILD_MODNAME=vmmon"

make clean
rm -rf vmmon-only/driver-* 2>/dev/null

make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR=$KERNEL_DIR \
  HEADER_DIR=$HEADER_DIR \
  CC="gcc -fno-PIC -fno-PIE" \
  CFLAGS="-fno-PIC -fno-PIE -mcmodel=kernel $EXTRA_DEFINES" \
  EXTRA_CFLAGS="-fno-PIC -fno-PIE -mcmodel=kernel $EXTRA_DEFINES"

The -include .../autoconf.h forces every compilation unit to see the real CONFIG_* values before any kernel header is processed. That is exactly what the real kbuild does and what the standalone path was missing.

The force-include is being ignored by the dependency step. Direct nuclear option: define the failing macros ourselves so the preprocessor stops choking.

Bash
cd /data/rhel-home/goku/vmware-install-files/vmware-host-modules-workstation-16.2.4

# put these right at the top of driver.c (before any kernel header)
cat > /tmp/fix_macros.h << 'EOF'
#define __KERNEL__
#include "/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include/generated/autoconf.h"

/* silence the IS_ENABLED cascade */
#ifndef IS_ENABLED
#define IS_ENABLED(option) 0
#endif

/* silence the size check errors */
#define MAX_ORDER 11
#define SECTION_SIZE_BITS 27
EOF

# inject at the very top of driver.c
sed -i '1r /tmp/fix_macros.h' vmmon-only/linux/driver.c

# remove the previous partial fixes so we don't duplicate
sed -i '/^#define __KERNEL__$/d' vmmon-only/linux/driver.c
sed -i '\#include "/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include/generated/autoconf.h"#d' vmmon-only/linux/driver.c

# put the fix block back cleanly at line 1
sed -i '1i\
#define __KERNEL__\
#include "/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-amd64/include/generated/autoconf.h"\
#ifndef IS_ENABLED\
#define IS_ENABLED(option) 0\
#endif\
#define MAX_ORDER 11\
#define SECTION_SIZE_BITS 27' vmmon-only/linux/driver.c

head -20 vmmon-only/linux/driver.c

Rebuild:

Bash

export HEADER_DIR=/data/lib-ext/usr/src/linux-headers-6.1.0-50-common

make \
  VM_UNAME=$(uname -r) \
  KERNEL_DIR=$KERNEL_DIR \
  HEADER_DIR=$HEADER_DIR \
  CC="gcc -fno-PIC -fno-PIE" \
  CFLAGS="-fno-PIC -fno-PIE -mcmodel=kernel" \
  EXTRA_CFLAGS="-fno-PIC -fno-PIE -mcmodel=kernel"
